material.text: 9月1日，沪宁合高铁、津潍高铁、渝万高铁三条时速350公里的高铁线路在同一天迎来铺轨关键节点。从长三角到环渤海再到成渝地区双城经济圈，三条钢铁大动脉同日迈入建设新阶段，为中国经济畅通“大动脉”写下生动注脚。 长三角铁路上新 都市圈间架起快速新通道 9月1日，沪宁合高铁全线铺轨正式启动，沪宁合高铁建设全面转入线上施工阶段。 作为国家“八纵八横”高速铁路网沿江通道的重要组成部分，沪宁合高铁是沪渝蓉沿江高铁的东段线路，起自上海市新建上海宝山站，经江苏省苏州市、南通市、泰州市、扬州市、南京市，以及安徽省滁州市、合肥市，接入既有合肥南站，线路全长约554公里，设计时速350公里，全线设16座车站。 沪宁合高铁建成通车后， 将在上海大都市圈、南京都市圈和合肥都市圈间建起一条快速新通道， 对于打造“轨道上的长三角”，优化沿长江地区铁路网布局，服务长江经济带发展，助力长三角一体化高质量发展等具有重要意义。 环渤海再添骨干线 津潍高铁铺轨全面启动 9月1日，随着津潍高铁滨州站、东营南站开始长轨铺设， 津潍高铁全面进入铺轨阶段。 津潍高铁是国家高速铁路网“八纵八横”主通道中京沪辅助通道、沿海通道的重要骨干线路，线路北起天津滨海站，南接济青高铁潍坊北站，正线全长348公里，设计运行时速350公里，全线设滨州站、东营南站、潍坊北站等10座客运车站，全线铺轨长度768公里，铺设有砟道岔28组、无砟道岔114组。 津潍高铁建成通车后，将进一步完善环渤海区域高速铁路骨干网络， 串联天津、沧州、滨州、东营、潍坊等沿线重点城市，打通京沪高铁辅助通道与沿海高铁通道互联互通关键节点， 对优化全国高速铁路网整体布局、助力京津冀协同发展、促进山东半岛城市群融合互通、赋能沿线城市经济社会高质量发展具有重要意义。 渝万高铁钢轨铺通 成渝双城经济圈再提速 9月1日，新建重庆至万州高速铁路（简称“渝万高铁”）钢轨全线铺通。 渝万高铁是我国“八纵八横”高铁网包（银）海、京昆通道的重要组成部分，也是沿江高铁辅助通道的重要组成部分。线路起自重庆东站，终至万州北站，正线全长251公里，设计时速350公里。全线铺轨工程（含站线）总里程约540公里，其中正线约520公里，站线约20公里，包含97组道岔铺设。 渝万高铁建成通车后， 将进一步密切渝东北三峡库区城镇群和主城都市区之间的联系，便利沿线人民群众出行， 促进沿线经济社会发展，对更好地服务成渝地区双城经济圈建设具有重要意义。 三条钢铁大动脉同步按下“快进键” 提速的不只是列车 更是沿线人流、物流、信息流的畅通循环 一张越织越密的交通网 正为畅通国内经济大循环铺就坚实轨道 责任编辑：迟晓涵

# High-Speed Rail Tracks Laid on the Same Day

On September 1, three high-speed railway lines started their tracklaying work. These lines are the Shanghai-Nanjing-Hefei, Tianjin-Weifang, and Chongqing-Wanzhou lines. Each line has a design speed of 350 kilometers per hour. This means trains can travel very fast on them.

The Shanghai-Nanjing-Hefei line starts at the new Shanghai Baoshan Station. It passes through Suzhou, Nantong, Taizhou, Yangzhou, and Nanjing in Jiangsu Province. Then it goes through Chuzhou and Hefei in Anhui Province. It ends at the existing Hefei South Station. The total length is about 554 kilometers. There are 16 stations along the line.

This line is an important part of the national high-speed railway network. It belongs to the Yangtze River corridor. This corridor is part of the 'Eight Vertical and Eight Horizontal' network. The line is also the eastern section of the Shanghai-Chongqing-Chengdu Yangtze River high-speed railway.

The Tianjin-Weifang line starts from Tianjin Binhai Station in the north. It connects to Weifang North Station in the south. That station is on the Jinan-Qingdao high-speed railway. The main line is 348 kilometers long. It has 10 passenger stations. These include Binzhou, Dongying South, and Weifang North.

The total tracklaying length for the Tianjin-Weifang line is 768 kilometers. This number includes 28 ballasted turnouts and 114 ballastless turnouts. Turnouts help trains change from one track to another. They are very important for railway safety.

This line is a key trunk line in the national network. It serves the Beijing-Shanghai auxiliary corridor and the coastal corridor. These corridors help connect big cities and coastal areas. They make travel easier for many people.

The Chongqing-Wanzhou line starts from Chongqing East Station. It ends at Wanzhou North Station. The main line is 251 kilometers long. Its design speed is also 350 kilometers per hour. The total tracklaying length is about 540 kilometers. This includes about 520 kilometers of main line and 20 kilometers of station lines. There are 97 turnouts.

This line is important for the 'Eight Vertical and Eight Horizontal' network. It is part of the Baotou-Yinchuan-Hainan and Beijing-Kunming corridors. It is also an auxiliary channel of the Yangtze River high-speed railway. This means it supports the main Yangtze River line.

Building these lines will help regional economies. Faster trains bring cities closer together. People can travel for work or business more easily. Goods can also move faster between regions. This helps create more jobs and trade.

The start of tracklaying on the same day shows strong progress. It shows that China is working hard to connect its regions. When these lines open, they will change how people live and work. They will also support long-term economic growth.

auxiliary — 辅助的
regional — 区域的

# High-Speed Rail Tracks Laid on the Same Day

On September 1, three high-speed railway lines with a design speed of 350 kilometers per hour—the Shanghai-Nanjing-Hefei, Tianjin-Weifang, and Chongqing-Wanzhou lines—officially started tracklaying on the same day. This coordinated start marks a significant milestone in China's efforts to strengthen regional connectivity and economic integration.

The Shanghai-Nanjing-Hefei high-speed railway begins at the new Shanghai Baoshan Station and passes through Suzhou, Nantong, Taizhou, Yangzhou, and Nanjing in Jiangsu Province, before continuing through Chuzhou and Hefei in Anhui Province. It terminates at the existing Hefei South Station. The line has a total length of about 554 kilometers and includes 16 stations along its route.

As part of the national 'Eight Vertical and Eight Horizontal' high-speed railway network, this line belongs to the Yangtze River corridor. It also forms the eastern section of the Shanghai-Chongqing-Chengdu Yangtze River high-speed railway. This positioning makes it a crucial artery linking the economically dynamic Yangtze River Delta with central and western China.

The Tianjin-Weifang high-speed railway starts from Tianjin Binhai Station in the north and extends southward to connect with Weifang North Station on the Jinan-Qingdao high-speed railway. The main line is 348 kilometers long and contains 10 passenger stations, including Binzhou, Dongying South, and Weifang North.

The total tracklaying length for the Tianjin-Weifang line is 768 kilometers, a figure that includes 28 ballasted turnouts and 114 ballastless turnouts. Turnouts are critical components that allow trains to switch between tracks safely and efficiently, and their installation requires precise engineering.

This railway functions as an important trunk line within the national network, serving both the Beijing-Shanghai auxiliary corridor and the coastal corridor. These corridors are designed to relieve pressure on existing lines while improving access between major northern cities and the eastern seaboard, thus facilitating both passenger travel and freight movement.

The Chongqing-Wanzhou high-speed railway starts from Chongqing East Station and ends at Wanzhou North Station. Its main line is 251 kilometers long, with a design speed of 350 kilometers per hour. The total tracklaying length is about 540 kilometers, comprising roughly 520 kilometers of main line and 20 kilometers of station lines, along with 97 turnouts.

This line is an important component of the Baotou-Yinchuan-Hainan and Beijing-Kunming corridors, both of which are part of the 'Eight Vertical and Eight Horizontal' network. Additionally, it serves as an auxiliary channel of the Yangtze River high-speed railway, thereby reinforcing the broader transport framework in southwest China.

From an economic perspective, these three projects will substantially enhance regional ties. Reduced travel times lower transaction costs and make it easier for businesses to operate across provincial boundaries. Cities along the routes are likely to attract more investment, while workers gain access to a wider range of job opportunities. Improved logistics also benefit industries that rely on timely delivery.

The fact that tracklaying began on the same day for all three lines underscores the coordinated pace of China's high-speed rail expansion. Once operational, these railways will not only improve daily travel but also contribute to more balanced regional development. They represent long-term investments in connectivity that align with broader economic planning goals.

# Exploring Chinese Breakfast Culture

Breakfast is often described as the most important meal of the day, and in China this idea takes on remarkable regional variety. Unlike many countries where breakfast options are relatively uniform, China offers a wide range of morning dishes that differ from province to province. Some of these specialties have gained international recognition. This article examines three notable Chinese breakfast items and the cultural traditions that surround them.

Wuhan hot dry noodles stand out as one of China's most distinctive breakfast foods. Originating in Wuhan, a major city in central China, this dish consists of noodles tossed in a rich sesame-based sauce, often with pickled vegetables and chili oil. It is a quick, filling meal that locals commonly eat before starting their workday. Over time, it has become an iconic representation of Wuhan's culinary identity.

In Southern China, particularly in Guangdong province, dim sum occupies a central place in breakfast culture. Traditionally eaten for breakfast or brunch, dim sum is more than just a meal. It is a social ritual in which families and friends gather at restaurants, share numerous small dishes, and spend hours talking and eating together. This communal aspect is essential to the dim sum experience.

The term dim sum is often used interchangeably with morning tea, which points to its historical roots. The tradition began in teahouses where travelers along ancient trade routes would stop to rest. They drank tea and consumed small portions of food, a practice known as yum cha, meaning drink tea in Cantonese. As time passed, the food offered at these teahouses became increasingly elaborate and central to the experience.

The 19th century marked a period of rapid growth for dim sum culture in Guangzhou. Chefs in the city began experimenting with diverse cooking techniques and a broader range of ingredients. This culinary innovation led to an explosion in the variety of dim sum dishes available. Teahouses evolved into bustling social hubs where people from different backgrounds came together to eat and converse.

One defining feature of dim sum is its presentation. Dishes are served on small plates, each containing two or three pieces. This format allows diners to taste a wide array of foods in one sitting without becoming overly full. It also reinforces the sharing nature of the meal, as everyone at the table can sample from the same plates.

Despite its strong association with breakfast, dim sum is remarkably versatile. It is commonly enjoyed for lunch, and some establishments serve it as a late-night snack. This adaptability has contributed to its enduring popularity in contemporary society, where eating schedules are often irregular. Dim sum fits into various parts of the day without losing its identity.

Mat, an enthusiast of Chinese breakfast cuisine, has identified three personal favorites: Wuhan hot dry noodles, rice noodle rolls, and steamed pork buns. He is particularly fond of the BBQ pork version of rice noodle rolls, which combines silky rice noodles with savory-sweet pork filling. For Mat, these dishes capture the breadth and depth of China's morning food traditions.

For comparison, a traditional English breakfast offers a stark contrast. It typically consists of eggs, bacon, sausage, and toast, and in many restaurants across England it is available throughout the day under the name All Day Breakfast. This all-day availability differs from most Chinese breakfast items, which are generally served only during morning hours, reflecting different cultural attitudes toward the first meal of the day.

Chinese breakfast culture is a vivid reflection of the country's regional diversity and historical depth. Every dish carries a story tied to a specific place and time. From the robust flavors of Wuhan's hot dry noodles to the refined variety of Guangdong's dim sum, these foods connect people to their heritage and to one another. In China, breakfast is far more than a simple meal. It is an expression of identity, community, and tradition.

title: US Strikes Iran, and Iran Strikes Back

material.label: Iran hits back after US launches new strikes
material.text:
Commercial vessels seen anchored in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran, August 5, 2026. /VCG

Multiple explosions were heard on Tuesday evening across Iran's southern Hormozgan and southeastern Sistan and Baluchestan provinces, as US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the start of strikes against targets belonging to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

Blasts were heard in the counties of Sirik, Bandar Abbas and Qeshm in Hormozgan, as well as Konarak and Chabahar in Sistan and Baluchestan, the semi-official Fars News Agency reported.

The exact locations and origins of the blasts remain unknown, it added.

Fars cited Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan's deputy governor for political and security affairs, as saying that at least five people, including a four-year-old child and a woman, were killed and over 50 others wounded in the US attack targeting the wedding ceremony in Sirik county.

The semi-official Tasnim News Agency, citing local sources, reported six blasts in Konarak and eight south of Qeshm Island, with unofficial accounts suggesting an explosion from the island's airport.

Meanwhile, Ali Khalilabadi, Sistan and Baluchestan's deputy governor for security and law enforcement affairs, said four projectiles hit Chabahar and Konarak, the semi-official Mehr News Agency reported.

In a Tuesday post on social media platform X, CENTCOM said US forces have begun striking IRGC targets. "The strikes follow recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members deployed to the region."

Tasnim also cited sources claiming that Iran had launched missiles toward US bases in regional countries, though the report has not been officially confirmed yet.

Iran's main military command, Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, said in a statement that in response to the US "air aggression," the Iranian armed forces will deal "crushing and shattering" blows to the United States.

The latest strikes have further escalated tensions in and around the Strait of Hormuz, with Washington and Tehran trading accusations and threats of further military action.

IRGC claims beginning retaliation for US strikes

The IRGC said on Tuesday night it has started strikes against US bases and assets in the region in retaliation for US attacks.

In a statement published on its official news outlet Sepah News, the IRGC said its "regret-inducing response against the aggressors" have begun, noting its air defense had shot down a "hostile" US MQ-9 Reaper drone.

Its aerospace forces also launched ballistic missile and drone strikes on Camp Titin in Jordan and Shaikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain, reportedly killing "a large number" of US troops and destroying several key facilities and combat helicopters.

It stressed that the US strikes will only protract the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and make the Iranian armed forces more determined to "suppress the foreign forces interfering in the waterway."

The IRGC said the attacks began after the United States bombed a number of civilian places in Iran's southern coasts "out of desperation" and in retaliation for the US "criminal" and deadly attack on a wedding ceremony in Hormozgan province.

The Jordanian Armed Forces-Arab Army (JAF) said later that the country's air defense systems on Tuesday evening intercepted and destroyed 10 of 13 ballistic missiles that entered the country's airspace from Iran in the past hours.

Three other missiles fell in remote areas away from population centers, with no casualties or loss of life reported, according to a JAF statement.

US President Donald Trump talks on the phone with crew members of the International Space Station at NASA's Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center in Houston, Texas, August 28, 2026. /VCG

Trump warns of 'much harder' action

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday commented on the US military strikes on Iran as "large and powerful" in a Truth Social post, and warned that Iran would courtface even greater strikes if it retaliated.

If Iran "retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level," Trump warned in a post on Truth Social.

"But it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings and, when it is over, there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran!" Trump threatened in the post.

In a phone interview with Fox News, he claimed US forces destroyed "a lot of radar" in Iran's network, including systems Tehran attempted to rebuild. "This is a very big hit today. If it goes a third time, they're going to be totally wiped out as a country," Trump said.

"The (USS) George Washington is loaded to the gills," he added. "We're loaded up."

Trump said Gulf allies were notified ahead of the latest strikes, according to a Fox News report.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei on Tuesday rejected as a "lie" the US claim that its recent attack on Iran's Larak Island was carried out because Iranian forces were preparing to lay mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
